config.description: v028's exact recipe with the ONE axis that has never been varied: the MLP head width. model.head_hidden 192 -> 384, so 225,922 -> 263,362 params (+16.5%). The recurrent trunk is untouched at hidden 128.
config.hypothesis:
The reasoning is that v028 finishes in 46m52s of a 60-minute budget, so 14 minutes are unspent, and capacity is the obvious thing to spend them on. That reasoning is right about the headroom and WRONG about which part to enlarge, and the distinction is the whole point of this run.
Per-row compute splits as: GRU1 44.0%, GRU0 33.0%, head 16.7%, projection 6.4%. So the recurrent trunk is 83.3% of the cost and the head is 16.7%. Every capacity experiment we have run spent on the trunk, and all of them lost:
  hidden 128 -> 285 (871,977 params): -2.2 sigma, and TIMED OUT on the grader
  hidden 128 -> 415 (1,742,717 params): -10.2 sigma, and TIMED OUT
Widening the trunk does not merely fail to help, it fails twice and costs the submission outright. dozken's own data agrees: his 384x2 teacher was +0.003 over 192x2, and his 872k scored the same as 436k.
The head has NEVER been varied, so it is the only place where "bigger" is both affordable and untested. Doubling it adds 16.5% compute against the trunk's 83.3%, so the grader projection moves from 78% of budget to roughly 86% -- still inside the limit, unlike the trunk changes which blew straight through it.
Prediction, and it is genuinely uncertain in a way the trunk runs were not: a wider readout may help, may do nothing, or may hurt. The trunk results give a reason to expect harm, since they suggest extra capacity in this problem is absorbed as overfitting rather than used. The counter is that the head is a different KIND of capacity -- it is where the t0/t1 readouts are formed, it consumes the skip from the 64-wide projection, and no trunk experiment ever touched it. If this returns within 0.000317 of v028 then head width is not a lever either, and combined with the trunk results that closes capacity as an axis entirely. If it returns worse by more than 0.000317, that is consistent and expected.
config.change_vs_parent: model.head_hidden 192 -> 384, and the script change that plumbs model.head_hidden through BOTH model construction sites (training and export) so train and serve cannot diverge. Verified: with no head_hidden key the constructor reproduces v028's 225,922 params exactly, so the plumbing itself is a no-op for every other run. hidden, input_proj, layers, dropout, distill_weight, gamma, chunk_len, epochs, teacher, schedule, LR and seed are all unchanged.
